Definition: an abode, of God (the Tabernacle or the Temple), men (their home) or animals (their lair); hence, a retreat (asylum)
BiblicalUsage: The word names a dwelling place, an abode, and it is used for the homes of men, the dens of beasts, and the habitation of God Himself. Moses asks God to look down from His holy habitation, from heaven, and bless His people Israel, and the psalm says the LORD has been our dwelling place in all generations. The psalmist calls God his strong habitation where he may continually resort, and Jeremiah hears the LORD roar from on high and utter His voice from His holy habitation.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe a dwelling is more than a house: it is where a person belongs, and God has made Himself our dwelling place. I hold that the one who lives in God is never homeless, because the holy habitation is not a building but the LORD Himself.
